title: Microsoft Teams lets you turn off AI mid-meeting | Traq Collective
h1: Microsoft Teams now lets you turn AI off mid-meeting
metaDescription: Since July 2026, Teams organizers and presenters can turn Copilot, Facilitator and Recap off during a live call, not just before it. What that means for your team.
targetQuery: how to turn off AI in a Microsoft Teams meeting
author: Nazir Dogan
dek: Copilot, Facilitator and Recap used to run by default. Now the organizer decides, mid-call.
intro: Microsoft Teams now lets meeting organizers and presenters turn Copilot, Facilitator and Recap on or off during a live call, not just before it starts. The toggle rolled out in July 2026 after user pushback over AI features running by default. It requires a Teams Premium or Microsoft 365 Copilot licence, and turning on transcription still activates the AI automatically.

body.heading: What changed in Microsoft Teams in July 2026
paragraphs: Until now, if your Teams meetings had Copilot, Facilitator or Recap switched on, that was a setting made before the call, usually by IT, and rarely revisited. Microsoft rolled out an in-meeting toggle in July 2026, after enough customers pushed back on AI features (especially Facilitator, which summarises and nudges the conversation as it happens) running without anyone in the room choosing that. Now an organizer or presenter can turn any of the three off, or back on, from the meeting controls menu, mid-call.

body.heading: Who can turn it off, and the transcription catch
paragraphs: Two details matter more than the headline. First, only organizers and presenters get the toggle, and it needs a Teams Premium or Microsoft 365 Copilot licence, so check who on your team actually has that access before you assume everyone can flip it. Second, transcription and AI are linked: starting a transcript switches Copilot and Recap on automatically, even if someone turned them off earlier. If a meeting needs to be genuinely AI-free, both transcription and the AI toggle have to be off, not just one.

body.heading: Decide as a team when AI should be off
paragraphs: The useful move here is not turning AI off everywhere. It is deciding, as a team, when it should be off, client calls where someone hasn't consented to being recorded or summarised, sensitive HR conversations, anything under an NDA, and making that a default rather than something one person remembers to click. Write it down as a one-line rule, tell the team, and check occasionally that new hires know it too.

takeaway: This week, name the two or three meeting types where AI notetaking should default to off (client calls, HR, anything under NDA) and tell your team which toggle controls it. Do not leave it to whoever remembers to click.

stat.claim: Microsoft added an in-meeting toggle so Teams organizers and presenters can turn Copilot, Facilitator and Recap off during a live call, not just before it starts, after customer pushback over AI running by default.

faqs.q: Can anyone in a Microsoft Teams meeting turn off Copilot or Recap?
faqs.a: No. Only the organizer or a presenter can use the toggle, and it requires a Teams Premium or Microsoft 365 Copilot licence. If you need AI off for a specific meeting, that has to be someone with the right role and licence, not any attendee.
